limits: Personal historical discovery/achievement claims were not independently checked and are not proof of current test performance.

claims: Company distinguishes several diagnostic offerings, including its CTR-Test and other named test services; the business is not a single undifferentiated assay.
limits: Distribution of another named test does not establish ownership or development of that test.
Patient-selection guidance is company material, not an independent clinical guideline.

claims: CTR-Test uses viable tumor material, exposes cells to selected chemotherapy agents, compares growth with untreated controls and reports to the physician; the page describes sample transport and laboratory processing.
limits: Detailed workflow inspected, not actual testing or current clinical/regulatory validation.
Headline accuracy, adoption counts and survival-benefit statements were not independently verified and must not be repeated as established outcomes.
Long reported availability warrants early-stage scope review; it is not an automatic age exclusion.

claims: The curated 1999 ovarian-cancer study summary explicitly notes nonrandomized patients and possible prognostic confounding; the page groups clinical and specimen-validation studies.
limits: Study counts and manufacturer-wide utility claims are not independently validated.
Correlation, specimen validation and treatment-guided survival benefit are distinct questions.
The external original-study link failed; this pass reviewed company-hosted summaries, not the original publication.
